parts.subtitle: One native bird in New Zealand that has managed to survive the introduction of non-native species
parts.article:
A survivor’s story
 
One native bird in New Zealand that has managed to survive the introduction of non-native species
 
(A) As an island country with a fauna dominated by birds, New Zealand was once home to an owl species which is now extinct, the laughing owl, named for its distinctive cry. This bird was widespread throughout the islands when European settlers arrived in the middle of the 19th century and it remained in good numbers for some years thereafter. Where other native birds suffered from predation by the Polynesian rat, the laughing owl turned the tables and adapted its diet to include the rodent. It was also capable of catching and killing the other New Zealand owl, the morepork, and even larger birds, such as the weka. However, the laughing owl was wiped out around the beginning of the 20th century, its demise caused by specimen collectors, habitat changes, and non-native predators including cats and stoats. Surprisingly, it is the smaller owl, the morepork, that has managed to survive until this day.
 
(B) Speckled dark brown, with yellow eyes and long tails, they are around 29 centimetres long from head to tail and 175 grams in weight. Moreporks have fringes on the edge of their feathers, so they can fly almost silently and not alert potential prey. They have acute hearing and their large eyes are very sensitive to light.
 
(C) Moreporks nest in tree hollows, in clumps of plants, or in cavities among rocks and roots. In the wild, moreporks usually start nesting in October, although two specimens have been recorded nesting in mid-winter, possibly stimulated by an ample food supply. The female lays up to three white eggs, which she incubates for 20 to 30 days. During this time, she rarely hunts, and the male brings food to her.
 
(D) Once the chicks hatch, she stays mainly on the nest until the young owls are fully feathered. When hatched, chicks are covered in light grey down and have their eyes closed. The eyes do not open until the eighth day after hatching. They can fly at around 35 days.
 
(E) By day, moreporks sleep in roosts. By night, they hunt a variety of animals – mainly large invertebrates including scarab and huhu beetles, moths, caterpillars and spiders. They also take small birds and mice. They can find suitable food in pine forest as well as native forest. A morepork uses its sharp talons to catch or stun its prey, which it then carries away in its bill. Moreporks are clever hunters, and birds such as robins, grey warblers and fantails can end up as their prey. In the day, these small birds sometimes mob drowsy moreporks and chase them away from their roosts; they force the sleepy predators to search for a more peaceful spot.
 
(F) Moreporks have proved to be ungracious hosts. Scientists trying to establish a population of plovers on Motuora Island in New Zealand’s Hauraki Gulf were mystified as to why only two birds survived out of the 75 placed there. The culprits turned out to be five pairs of moreporks that ate or chased away the new arrivals.
 
(G) Although moreporks are still considered to be relatively common, it is likely that numbers are in gradual decline due to predation and loss of habitat. As the female is a hole-nester, she is vulnerable to predators such as stoats and possums during the breeding season, and eggs and chicks will also be at risk from rats. The use of pesticides is another possible threat to the owls, though not a direct one. As moreporks are at the top of the food chain, they could be affected by an accumulative poison by consuming prey that has ingested poison.
 
(H) The New Zealand Department of Conservation is taking steps to ensure the preservation of New Zealand’s only native owl. The department is involved in measuring the population of moreporks and has put transmitters on a number of birds to determine survival and mortality. As well as being New Zealand’s only native owl, the morepork has symbolic and spiritual importance, so in monitoring the birds it is hoped that the morepork will continue to survive and thrive.
 
(I) At dusk, the melancholy sound of the morepork can be heard in forests and parks as it calls to other moreporks and claims territory. Its Māori name (ruru) echoes its two-part cry. In the tradition of the Māori people of New Zealand, the morepork, or ruru, was often seen as a careful guardian. A number of sayings referred to the bird’s alertness. As a bird of the night, it was associated with the spirit world. Moreporks were believed to act as messengers to the gods in the heavens, flying along spiritual paths in the sky. They were the mediums used to communicate with the gods. The occasional high, piercing call of the morepork signified bad news, but the lower-pitched and more common “ruru” call heralded good news.

questions.question: Early European settlers made detailed studies of the morepork.

analyses.content: 不要看到“European settlers”（欧洲定居者）出现了就觉得是 TRUE，要看他们具体“做了什么”，文中没说他们做研究。
(A段) This bird was widespread throughout the islands when European settlers arrived in the middle of the 19th century and it remained in good numbers for some years thereafter.
文中第一段提到了欧洲定居者的到来和猫头鹰数量的变化，但从未提及他们对 Morepork（Morepork）进行了“详细的研究（detailed studies）”。

questions.question: The Polynesian rat had a negative effect on the number of laughing owls.

analyses.content: 文中明确说笑鸮（laughing owl）“扭转了局势（turned the tables）”，把波利尼西亚鼠变成了自己的食物，而不是受老鼠影响变少。
看到“suffered from predation”（遭受捕食）不要急着选 TRUE，那是“other native birds”（其他本地鸟类）的遭遇，不是笑鸮的。
(A段) Where other native birds suffered from predation by the Polynesian rat, the laughing owl turned the tables and adapted its diet to include the rodent.

questions.question: The laughing owl was larger than the morepork.

analyses.content: 文中提到 Morepork 是“the smaller owl（较小的猫头鹰）”，这直接暗示了已经灭绝的笑鸮（laughing owl）体型更大。
题目是反着说的“笑鸮比 Morepork 大”，而文中是说“Morepork 是较小的那个”，逻辑一致，不要因为没看到“laughing owl is larger”就选 NG。
(A段) Surprisingly, it is the smaller owl, the morepork, that has managed to survive until this day.

questions.question: Rats pose a risk to young moreporks.

analyses.content: 题目中的“young moreporks”对应文中的“chicks”，含义完全对应。
文中 G 段明确指出，Morepork 的蛋和幼鸟（chicks）会面临来自老鼠（rats）的风险。
(G段) ...and eggs and chicks will also be at risk from rats.

questions.question: The New Zealand Department of Conservation is hoping to limit the population of moreporks.

analyses.content: 环保部的目的是确保其“preservation”（保护）并希望它们“survive and thrive”（生存繁衍），这与“limit”（限制数量）完全相反。
你可能看到了 Department of Conservation 就在做“measuring the population”（测量种群数量），但这不等于限制数量。
(H段) The New Zealand Department of Conservation is taking steps to ensure the preservation of New Zealand’s only native owl... it is hoped that the morepork will continue to survive and thrive.

questions.question: Other bird species are frightened away when they hear the morepork’s cry.

analyses.content: 文中提到 Morepork 的叫声可以宣示领地（claims territory），也提到白天小鸟会围攻它，但从未说其他鸟听到叫声会“被吓跑（frightened away）”。
虽然它是捕食者，但不要主观臆断其他鸟听到声音就会怕，文中没给这个信息。
(I段) At dusk, the melancholy sound of the morepork can be heard in forests and parks as it calls to other moreporks and claims territory.

questions.question: In Māori tradition, the low call of the morepork had negative associations.

analyses.content: (I段) The occasional high, piercing call of the morepork signified bad news, but the lower-pitched and more common “ruru” call heralded good news.
文中确实提到了“bad news”，那是对应“high, piercing call”（尖锐的高音），看清题目问的是“low call”。
文中最后一句明确说，低沉的“ruru”叫声预示着“good news”（好消息），而不是负面联想。

analyses.content: 文中 B 段开头提到它们身长约为“29 centimetres”，填单位词。
(B段) Speckled dark brown, with yellow eyes and long tails, they are around 29 centimetres long from head to tail...
文中 C 段列举了筑巢地点：树洞、植物丛、以及“rocks and roots”（岩石和树根）之间的空洞。
题目中 roots 已经给出了，并列的另一个地点就是 rocks，不要漏看。
(C段) Moreporks nest in tree hollows, in clumps of plants, or in cavities among rocks and roots.
文中 E 段提到 Morepork 抓住猎物后，会用它的“bill”（鸟喙/嘴）把猎物带走。
你可能想填 talons（爪子），但文中说的是用 talons 抓或击晕，用 bill 搬运（carries away）。
(E段) A morepork uses its sharp talons to catch or stun its prey, which it then carries away in its bill.
文中提到在“In the day”（白天），小鸟会围攻昏昏欲睡的 Morepork 并把它们赶走。
题目问的是时间段“during the...”，直接对应原文的 In the day。
(E段) In the day, these small birds sometimes mob drowsy moreporks and chase them away from their roosts...
文中 F 段提到科学家试图建立“plovers”（鸻鸟）的种群，结果被 Morepork 吃掉或赶跑了。
找被攻击的对象，定位到 Motuora Island 就能看到 plovers 这个词。
(F段) Scientists trying to establish a population of plovers on Motuora Island in New Zealand’s Hauraki Gulf...
文中 G 段末尾提到，Morepork 作为食物链顶端，可能会因为吃下含有“poison”（毒药）的猎物而受影响。
题目问的是“exposed to... in their prey”，对应原文“consuming prey that has ingested poison”。
(G段) ...they could be affected by an accumulative poison by consuming prey that has ingested poison.
